text:
The Kings arrive on the second night of a back-to-back and the last stop of a five-game road trip (3-1-0 so far), fresh off a 6-3 win at the Rangers. They're without Mats Zuccarello, who had 54 points in 59 games last season and is on injured reserve. Joel Armia has taken his spot beside Haula and Laferriere, and Erik Gustafsson has moved onto the first power-play unit. Chicago has lost three straight and was outscored 11-3 in that stretch, but Bowen Byram is now day-to-day and could return.

Our numbers say the Blackhawks are better than their record. They've taken 40% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five, against 48% for Los Angeles, yet sit at a -19 goal difference on -9.0 expected, with poor finishing and goaltending to blame. Both teams create about the same on the power play (0.51 expected goals a game), but the Kings take 4.1 penalties a game. In net, projected starters Anton Forsberg (LAK) and Spencer Knight (CHI) are both slightly negative in goals saved above expected (the goals a goalie saves beyond what the shot quality predicts) this season, though both were well positive last year.

Watch Artemi Panarin, 72% for a point and facing his former team's rival in a Kings sweater, and Connor Bedard, also 72%. As Scott Powers of The Athletic posted, Bertuzzi replaces Kane on Bedard's line. Our under-the-radar pick is Roman Kantserov, at 54% for a point, well above his season pace (36%), because his line creates chances.
